A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, including appendices, are readable; the retained text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression, transfer-learning, and reconstruction experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B.8.

after.justification: v3 retains original synthetic experiments and adds image-classification and feature-subspace analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix B.8 adds an alternative second-stage initialization in Lemma B.40, constructing 2(L+2) points from paired positive and negative scalar multiples of a direction. The existing two-stage procedure, GM/PM updates, and analyzed network remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic single- and multi-index regression and transfer tasks. v3 retains these and adds actual image-classification experiments on MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR10 in Appendix E, substantially broadening empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same full-data training, teacher training, Random I/II, and one-step GM/PM comparisons. Appendix E applies gradient matching without introducing comparisons against additional competing distillation methods.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces ConvNet classification protocols, accuracy and feature-subspace overlap measurements, and sweeps over distilled size, training size, and network width. Figure 2 also extends the log_d(n) range from 3 to 4 and adds the log N = log J* = 5 condition; these are additions to the retained synthetic setup.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a direct analysis relating feature-subspace preservation to classification accuracy and practical sensitivity tests for distilled size, training size, and width. Figure 2 extends the transfer-learning resource analysis. The reconstruction analysis in Figure 3 already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Figures 1–2 retain means and standard deviations over five seeds. The new image sweeps also report five-seed means, without introducing increased repetitions, confidence intervals, or significance testing. Additional results do not establish a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 2 replaces the earlier MSE curves and adds another resource condition; the PDFs do not explain the substantially different losses at overlapping plotted settings. Appendix E adds classification and overlap results: for example, Table 5 reports CIFAR10 accuracy increasing from 0.28 to 0.54 and overlap from 0.27 to 0.66 as distilled size increases from 10 to 500.

T1.justification: New Lemma B.40 and its proof provide a constructive almost-sure full-rank guarantee for the active rows under a nonzero-projection condition. This substantially strengthens Appendix B.8 beyond v1's maximal-attainable-rank result and heuristic constructions, addressing how the second-stage regularity requirement can be satisfied. The main generalization and memory bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding claims retain the same central results: gradient-based distillation encodes low-dimensional task structure and achieves memory complexity of approximately r²d + L. The additions support these claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 adds a qualified interpretation concerning deeper networks and cross-architecture transfer, connects the retained ReLU update to practical autodifferentiation conventions, and interprets the new overlap results as supporting structural preservation. The acknowledged limits of the two-layer, multi-index analysis remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly documents a three-layer ReLU ConvNet with average pooling and group normalization, using Zhao et al. (2021) defaults unless stated otherwise. This adds limited implementation information for the new experiments; the existing algorithm specification and hyperparameter summary are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Pope et al. (2021) to motivate intrinsic-dimensionality differences and cites Zhao and Bilen (2023) and Gu et al. (2024) when explaining excluded distillation families. The principal positioning against earlier distillation theory is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most wording and the main section sequence are retained. Changes consist of localized clarifications, additional discussion paragraphs, an Impact Statement, and Appendix E, rather than extensive rewriting or narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one column to two, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Figure 2 is redrawn; Tables 3–4 tabulate the existing Figure 3, and Tables 5–7 present new experiments. Tables 3–4 contain inconsistent L/M1 headings relative to Figure 3's distilled-size sweep.

improvement.justification: Lemma B.40 strengthens the justification for second-stage initialization, and Appendix E provides practical evidence for the retained structural and scaling interpretations. These are meaningful gains, but their overall benefit is limited by sparse documentation of the new overlap measurement, inconsistent Tables 3–4 headings, and unexplained changes to Figure 2's existing loss curves.
